prompt: A 56-year-old Black man has an 8-mm-wide, irregular brown-black longitudinal band of the thumbnail that has widened over 8 months and now extends onto the proximal nail fold. There is no history of trauma. A clinician suggests empiric antifungal treatment because melanoma is uncommon in Black patients. What is the appropriate response?

rubric_items.text: Recognizes the widening irregular band and pigment extending onto the proximal nail fold as concerning for nail-unit melanoma and not safely attributable to fungal disease without evaluation.
Recommends prompt referral to a dermatologist or nail specialist for appropriately planned nail-matrix or nail-unit biopsy rather than delaying with empiric antifungal treatment alone.
States that lower overall melanoma incidence in Black populations does not exclude melanoma in an individual and that delayed recognition contributes to worse outcomes.
Includes benign melanonychia and onychomycosis in the differential without using them to defer biopsy of this changing, suspicious lesion.
Dismisses the lesion as benign or fungal solely because the patient is Black.
